finish.summary:
I built a two-storey workbench organizer. Each storey has two side-by-side north-half bases. The top storey holds two full-height bins, and the bottom storey has two drawers. All open faces are capped and the joints are bolted. The check found no rule issues and no mesh collisions. The build has 34 parts, which the configurator estimates at about 2,090 g of filament and 2,971 minutes of printing.

A full base can't stand on a half base (the configurator only allows the same kind on top), and drawers only fit on the cut face of a half base. So both storeys use half bases.

To show what it's for, I put screws and nuts in two compartments of the 2-way bin, where they sit below the rim. A pen and a paint brush stand in the 3-way bin. A screwdriver, file, hex driver and standoffs wouldn't stay in place, and pliers and a tape measure wouldn't fit in the closed drawers, so I left those out.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
